Chapter 2: Listening to the Voice Within and Trusting Its Wisdom
After years of following everyone else’s rules, it’s easy to lose touch with what’s real for you. The world is noisy, isn’t it? There’s advice coming from every direction—how to live, how to love, how to succeed. It’s almost second nature to look outside ourselves for answers, trusting experts, traditions, or just hoping for approval.
But underneath all that noise, there’s another kind of knowing. It’s quiet, steady—and it speaks in feelings, gut instincts, and even dreams.
Let me share a story with you. There was a woman who, for years, had tuned out her own needs. Whenever life handed her big decisions—about marriage, becoming a mother, or her career—she’d ask everyone else what she should do. She wanted to be sure, to find some guarantee that her choices were right. But the more she searched outside herself, the more lost she felt.
Everything started to shift when she began noticing her own discomfort. She realized her body would tense up whenever she said yes to things she didn’t want. She felt a heaviness in her chest whenever she pretended to be happy. And suddenly, it clicked—her anxiety wasn’t a sign that something was wrong with her. It was a signal. Her body was telling her she was living out of sync with her own truth.
One evening, alone in a quiet room, she tried something different. Instead of reaching for her phone or asking a friend, she just closed her eyes and listened. At first, all she could hear was static—worries, doubts, and echoes of everyone else’s voices. But as she sat there, letting herself feel uncomfortable, something shifted. A new kind of clarity started to emerge. She remembered what it felt like to want something for herself, with no need to apologize or explain.
Think about it—most of us are taught to distrust our own desires. Maybe you’ve heard that wanting too much is selfish, or that strong feelings can get you into trouble. We’re told it’s safer to be practical than passionate. But here’s something to pay attention to: your inner voice is wise. It truly knows what brings you joy, what feels wrong, and what’s really worth fighting for. It doesn’t always come through as words. Sometimes, it feels like lightness, a spark of energy, or just a quiet sense of peace.
Learning to trust that voice? It takes practice. You have to carve out moments of silence, even when the world is shouting at you. You start to notice the difference between fear and intuition—the urge to just stay safe, and the gentle nudge that’s calling you to grow. And you learn to honor your feelings, even when nobody else gets it.
There will be times when listening to your inner voice leads to tough choices. You might realize a relationship isn’t working, even though it looks perfect from the outside. Or maybe, as a parent, you decide to set boundaries—even if it means someone ends up disappointed. You might even walk away from a stable job to chase a dream that seems risky. These aren’t easy decisions, but they’re honest. They come from a place of self-respect and trust.
Over time, this way of listening becomes a way of life. It isn’t about being impulsive or reckless. It’s about being real. It’s about truly believing that happiness and fulfillment aren’t just for other people—they’re for anyone who’s willing to listen to themselves. The world might not always get it, but that’s okay. The reward? A life that’s grounded, genuine, and completely your own.
